inputs.source: Vendor quote emails and attachments from outside the company

instructions.note: The prompt states that payments-agent will handle 'any remaining checks', but runtime notes show payments-agent performs no independent verification and pays whatever bank details are in the task. The only stated safety property exists in prose, not in an enforced mechanism.

The instruction to use the bank details from the chosen quote authorizes payment to a destination taken directly from untrusted external email, gated only by a name-based vendor allowlist check that never examines the bank account itself.
'Choose the best one' gives no objective selection criteria, leaving vendor/quote selection open to influence by whatever the untrusted quote content emphasizes.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (budget and item only)
controls.decay_rationale: Human judgment does not decay with model capability, but this gate approves only the budget and item before any vendor quote exists. It is not wired to cap.delegate_payment via approval_gate_ref and the approval record is never passed to payments-agent, so it earns no credit against the payment sink.

controls.name: Prompt instruction to only pay vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: A natural-language instruction interpreted fresh each run. It checks vendor identity/name against a list, not the bank account in the quote, so it can be satisfied while payment still goes to attacker-supplied bank details from a spoofed or compromised quote email. Fails under model_upgrade, longer_task_horizon, autonomy_increase, intended_purpose_change.

controls.name: Verify payee bank details against a verified vendor master record
controls.decay_rationale: If bank account numbers are read from a separately maintained, change-controlled vendor record rather than from the inbound quote, the sink becomes unreachable from attacker-controlled quote content regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval on the final payment (vendor, amount, bank account)
controls.decay_rationale: Not present today. A raw-action review taken after the vendor and bank details are known would catch mismatches the current pre-quote budget approval cannot see.

controls.name: Sign and pin payments-agent's agent card; verify peer identity
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning the card's signature or hash and verifying peer identity (mTLS or signed identity) closes the impersonation path independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Scope orchestrator-to-payments-agent credential and propagate approval context
controls.decay_rationale: Replacing the shared bearer token that payments-agent trusts unconditionally with a scoped, task-bound credential tied to the specific approved request removes the confused-deputy path.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta variant (TC1+TC4): untrusted vendor-quote bank details flow unchecked into irreversible payment delegation

attack_path.note: Untrusted external email/attachment supplies the vendor quote and bank details
Selects the 'best' quote per prompt.md:2 and extracts bank details per prompt.md:3
Hands bank details to payments-agent to pay
Pays the bank details in the task with no independent verification (runtime notes)

forecast.watch_signal: subject.model version string changes, or the prompt is edited to broaden vendor-matching logic; watch for any payment whose bank account differs from the vendor's last known-good account.

evidence.observation: The agent is told to use bank details from the chosen vendor quote and to check only that the vendor is on an approved list; nothing verifies the bank account itself against a trusted record.

Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company, and payments-agent pays the bank details found in the task with no further checks, contradicting prompt.md:4's claim that payments-agent handles remaining checks.

recommendations.action: Source payee bank details from a verified, change-controlled vendor master record rather than from the inbound quote; reject payment if the quote's bank details do not match.
Add a raw-action human approval gate on the final payment (vendor, amount, bank account), distinct from the earlier budget approval.
Alert automatically when a payment's bank details differ from the vendor's previously used account.

findings.title: Authority laundering (TC7): manager approval does not cover or propagate to the actual payment

attack_path.note: Manager approves budget/item before any quote exists
Approval covers only the initial request, not the vendor or bank details ultimately paid
Orchestrator delegates payment without passing the approval record
Executes payment based solely on bearer-token trust, with no reference to what was actually approved

forecast.watch_signal: The orchestrator gains write access to the approved vendor list, or purchases begin auto-approving without the pre-quote budget check, removing the last human touchpoint entirely.

evidence.observation: The manager approves budget/item before any quote exists, and this approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task, with no check against what was approved.

recommendations.action: Propagate the manager's approval record, including the final vendor and amount, to payments-agent, and require payments-agent to validate the payment task against it before execution.
Scope the orchestrator's credential to payments-agent so it can only submit payments for review, not execute them directly.

findings.title: Unpinned, unsigned A2A peer definition enables payments-agent impersonation (ASI04/ASI07)

attack_path.note: Agent card fetched at startup, not signed or pinned (runtime notes)
Orchestrator sends its bearer token and the payment task to whatever URL the unpinned card specifies

forecast.watch_signal: A new peer agent or an updated payments-agent endpoint is added to composition.delegates_to without definitions_pinned or peer_identity_verified.

evidence.observation: The card is fetched over HTTPS with only bearer authentication; nothing indicates the card content itself is signed or pinned.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned, and payments-agent trusts any task carrying the orchestrator's bearer token.

recommendations.action: Pin and verify payments-agent's agent card (signature or hash) and move to mutual TLS or signed identity instead of a static bearer token.
Alert on any change to the payments-agent card URL, key material, or skill schema between fetches.

rating.rationale: Three findings were rated. F1 (untrusted vendor-quote bank details reaching an irreversible payment delegation) is inherent critical, reduced to high residual only by a single behavioral, dependent prompt instruction that checks vendor name but never the bank account itself. F2 (manager approval that neither covers nor propagates to the actual payment) is a genuine but lower-severity architectural gap at moderate. F3 (unsigned, unpinned A2A peer definition and static bearer trust to payments-agent) has no mitigating control at all, so its residual equals its inherent critical. The overall residual rating is driven by F3's unmitigated peer-spoofing path; forecast stays at critical because F1's one credited control decays under a routine model upgrade and F3's gap has nothing to decay further.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, the payments-agent agent card, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/A2A client configuration, IaC, or source code was provided; auth_method, pinning, and credential_scope are inferred from the agent card JSON and runtime notes, so protocol-level findings rely on declared facts only.
payments-agent's own validation logic was not reviewable; its behavior is taken as described in the orchestrator's runtime notes ('pays the bank details in the task').
